podcast.body: "Dear God" was written by Andy Partridge for the Skylarking album (produced by Todd Rundgren). Everyone involved — Partridge, Rundgren, and Virgin Records — agreed it should not be picked as the single, with Partridge calling it "an arrogant attempt to sum up man's relationship with God in just 3.5 minutes," and Virgin disliking the whiny child at the opening. It was dropped from the album entirely and relegated to B-side on the 7-inch and 12-inch of "Grass" (August 26, 1986). "Grass" bombed completely. Radio stations flipped the single and played "Dear God" instead; listener response was massive. XTC's American label called England in panic. The album was repressed with the track restored; it sold a quarter million copies. Religious groups protested; a Florida radio station received a bomb threat; an 18-year-old student in Birmingham, New York named Gary Pulles held a knife to a school secretary demanding the song be played over the PA repeatedly. "As a result, the record started to sell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was initially an orphaned, non-album track recorded for the "Skylarking" album but excluded due to its anti-religious message. It was first released as the B-side to the single "Grass," where it gained popularity among college DJs. Its unexpected success led to its inclusion on later pressings of the "Skylarking" album, replacing "Mermaid Smile," and eventually becoming one of the band's biggest hits. "Dear God from XTC once an outtake B side, but later one of the biggest hits the band ever had."
